top_choice_rationale: P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) credits three separable contributions: the time-dependent pricing friction, staggered contracts with the policy rule, and the micro-founded welfare-based synthesis. The work is mature, has been used and revised through 2008, the zero lower bound and the post-2021 inflation, and no earlier prize recognised this core. My main round-1 objection was attribution. A citation naming these three components and not claiming the estimated-DSGE tradition largely answers it, though the exclusion of Galí, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets, Wouters and Gertler remains a real cost. I weigh breadth of tested influence and the workable component-based citation, not the number of supporters. P002 (Kiyotaki and Moore) has the cleanest attribution and is a distinct mechanism from the 2022 prize, so it is a strong second. Either award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for P001 or P002. I am a political scientist with no listed link to Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Kiyotaki or Moore. My co-authored Governance paper with Torsten Persson relates to B032, which is not in the proposal slate, and I rely on colleagues' accounts of the macro literature.
